micro_topic: ひとり暮らしで備えたい夏の暑さ対策
spoken_flow_summary: Hook (familiar summer room) → Why indoor heat matters (stats, calm framing) → Check 1: Room temperature & AC (practical tips) → Check 2: Hydration habits → Check 3: Body signals & when to act → Reaching out for help → Calm reassuring close

outline_sections.title_hint: 真夏の午後、部屋の温度を見ていますか
outline_sections.spoken_intent: Start with a quiet, familiar summer afternoon scene. A warm room, curtains half-drawn. Pose a soft question about whether the viewer has checked room temperature today. Establish the tone: calm, practical, no alarm.
key_points: Familiar domestic scene — afternoon, warm room
Soft opening question: 「今日、部屋の温度を確認しましたか？」
Transition: this video will organize 3 check areas for summer comfort
outline_sections.policy_notes: No fear framing. Warm domestic opening.
outline_sections.visual_scene_hint: Japanese apartment living room, thermometer on wall, soft afternoon light, curtains

outline_sections.title_hint: 室内の暑さは気づきにくい
outline_sections.spoken_intent: Explain why indoor heat is surprisingly dangerous for seniors. Use FDMA statistics calmly (97,578 transports, 57.4% seniors, 38% at home). Explain the perception gap — seniors feel less heat. Mention AC underuse reasons empathetically (cost, discomfort, habit).
key_points: F1: 2024年 熱中症搬送97,578人、過去最多。65歳以上が57.4%
F2: 発生場所「住居」38.0% — 室内が最多
F4: エアコンを使わない理由 — 電気代、不快感、暑さを感じにくい
Calm framing: 「〜ということが分かっています」tone
Transition: so let's organize 3 areas you can check at home
outline_sections.policy_notes: Policy warning: use statistics calmly, no fear theater. 「分かっています」「報告されています」の事実紹介トーン.
outline_sections.visual_scene_hint: Illustrated data card, apartment interior with warm tones, possibly thermometer showing high reading

outline_sections.title_hint: ひとつめ：部屋の温度と湿度を整える
outline_sections.spoken_intent: First check area: room temperature and humidity. Cover the 28-degree guideline (with softener MS1 — it's a guideline, not absolute). Humidity 40–60%. Recommend a thermometer-hygrometer. AC usage tips — prioritize health over cost. Low-cost alternatives: sudare, shading curtains, ventilation timing (morning/night), fan + AC combo. Address cost anxiety directly and empathetically.
key_points: F5: 「室温28度」は目安。設定温度≠室温。体調に合わせて調整
F6: 湿度40–60%。湿度80%超は28度でもリスク
G1: 温湿度計を設置して数値で確認
G2: エアコンは健康を守る道具。電気代より体調優先
G3: 遮光対策 — すだれ・よしず・遮光カーテン
G4: 換気タイミング — 早朝・夜間に開け、日中は閉める
G5: 扇風機・サーキュレーター併用
U3: 電気代比較は断定せず「〜とも言われています」
MS1 softener: 「あくまで目安です」
outline_sections.policy_notes: MS1 mandatory softener after temperature numbers. U3: no definitive AC cost claim. Empathetic cost-anxiety framing.
outline_sections.visual_scene_hint: AC remote control, thermometer-hygrometer on table, sudare on window, curtains

outline_sections.title_hint: ふたつめ：水分のとり方を見直す
outline_sections.spoken_intent: Second check area: hydration habits. Cover daily target (1,000–1,500ml outside meals, with MS2 softener). Timing: wake-up, meals, bath, bedtime. Preferred drinks: barley tea, water. Mention oral rehydration solution for heavy sweating. Coffee/alcohol are not substitutes. Food-based hydration: miso soup, fruit, jelly. Practical tip: keep a water bottle within reach.
key_points: F7: 食事以外の水分目安 1,000–1,500ml/日。コップ1杯200mlずつ
F7: タイミング — 起床時・食事時・入浴前後・就寝前
G6: 麦茶・水が基本。大量発汗時は経口補水液。コーヒー・アルコール不可
G7: 食事からの水分 — 味噌汁・果物・ゼリー
G9: 手の届く場所に飲み物を置く
MS2 softener: 「一般的な目安です。持病のある方はかかりつけ医に」
outline_sections.policy_notes: MS2 mandatory softener after fluid intake numbers. Acknowledge medical conditions requiring different intake.
outline_sections.visual_scene_hint: Kitchen table with water bottle, cup of barley tea, small notepad, miso soup bowl

outline_sections.title_hint: みっつめ：体の変化サインに気づく
outline_sections.spoken_intent: Third check area: recognizing early body signals. List self-checkable signs: dizziness, fatigue, leg cramps, headache, unusual sweating patterns. Emphasize that seniors often don't notice these early. What to do: rest in a cool place, cool the body (neck, armpits), drink water. When to call for help: symptoms don't improve, can't drink by yourself. MS3 softener after symptom list.
key_points: F8: 初期サイン — めまい・倦怠感・足のつり・頭痛・発汗異常・意識のぼんやり
G8: 体を冷やす — 首筋・脇の下・太ももの付け根に保冷剤・濡れタオル
C1: 休息後も改善しない → かかりつけ医・相談窓口に連絡
C2: 意識がぼんやり、自力で水分摂れない → 迷わず救急
MS3 softener: 「気になる症状が続く場合は、無理せず医療機関に」
Tone: calm awareness, not panic checklist
outline_sections.policy_notes: MS3 mandatory softener. VR1: no depiction of collapsed person. VR4: expression stays calm/mildly concerned. Consult-a-clinician framing required.
outline_sections.visual_scene_hint: Elderly person resting in chair, hand on forehead, calm living room, cooling items nearby

outline_sections.title_hint: まわりの力も借りましょう
outline_sections.spoken_intent: Encourage connecting with support systems. Mention community resources: 地域包括支援センター, 民生委員, neighbor check-ins. Municipal support: AC subsidies, cool shelters (涼み処), heat prevention goods distribution. Gentle encouragement: it's okay to ask for help. Not isolationist self-reliance.
key_points: Community_support: 地域包括支援センター、民生委員の訪問・安否確認
G10: 自治体のエアコン補助・涼み処・冷却グッズ配布
C3: 持病のある方 → 水分量は主治医に確認
Gentle encouragement: 「まわりに相談することも、大切な暑さ対策です」
outline_sections.policy_notes: Help-seeking framing. No shame for needing assistance.
outline_sections.visual_scene_hint: Neighbor waving from doorway, community center scene, bulletin board

outline_sections.title_hint: ひとつずつ、少しずつ整えていきましょう
outline_sections.spoken_intent: Quick recap of 3 check areas: (1) room temperature, (2) hydration, (3) body signals. Reassuring message: you don't need to do everything at once. Small steps make a difference. MS4 general disclaimer woven naturally. Warm farewell.
key_points: Recap: 3つのポイント — 部屋の温度・水分・体のサイン
Reassurance: 「全部を一度にやらなくても大丈夫です」
MS4 softener: 「この動画は一般的な情報です。個別のことはかかりつけ医にご相談ください」
Warm farewell: 「今年の夏も、穏やかに過ごせますように」
outline_sections.policy_notes: MS4 mandatory softener integrated naturally into closing. Calm, reassuring tone.
outline_sections.visual_scene_hint: Peaceful apartment interior, gentle evening light, organized and comfortable space
